result.topic_en: Corollaries showing that a sum of two squares admits no divisor of the form 4n−1 (unless both squares share it), and listing which quotients can arise when such a sum is divided by a prime of the form 4n+1.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 117
additum ſummam producat per numerum primum
$4n-1$ diuiſibilem.

Coroll. 1.

66. Summa ergo duorum quadratorum nul-
lum diuiſorem admittit formae $4n-1$; etiamſi hic
diuiſor non ſit primus, quoniam tum inter eius fa-
ctores ſemper vnus ſaltem primus formae $4n-1$
contineretur; niſi forte ambo quadrata ſeorſim per
eum fuerint diuiſibilia.

Coroll. 2.

67. Quando ergo ſumma duorum quadratorum
per numerum primum formae $4n+1$ eſt diuiſibi-
lis, quotus inde reſultans neque erit formae $4n-1$,
neque vllum habebit factorem primum huius formae,
niſi forte ambo quadrata huiusmodi habuerint com-
munem diuiſorem, quo caſu quotus adeo quadratum
talis numeri contineret.

Coroll. 3.

68. Ex ordine quotorum ergo, qui ſupra ex
diuiſione ſummae binorum quadratorum per nume-
rum primum formae $4n+1$ ſunt orti, excludun-
tur hi numeri
$3, 6, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15, 19, 21, 22, 23, 24, 27, 28, 30, 31$ etc.
ac propterea relinquuntur iſti tantum:

P 3 Pro-

items.quote: Summa ergo duorum quadratorum nullum diuiſorem admittit formae $4n-1$; etiamſi hic diuiſor non ſit primus, quoniam tum inter eius factores ſemper vnus ſaltem primus formae $4n-1$ contineretur; niſi forte ambo quadrata ſeorſim per eum fuerint diuiſibilia.
items.english: Therefore a sum of two squares admits no divisor of the form 4n−1, even if this divisor is not prime, since then among its factors at least one prime of the form 4n−1 would always be contained; unless perhaps both squares are separately divisible by it.

items.quote: Quando ergo ſumma duorum quadratorum per numerum primum formae $4n+1$ eſt diuiſibilis, quotus inde reſultans neque erit formae $4n-1$, neque vllum habebit factorem primum huius formae, niſi forte ambo quadrata huiusmodi habuerint communem diuiſorem, quo caſu quotus adeo quadratum talis numeri contineret.
items.english: When therefore a sum of two squares is divisible by a prime of the form 4n+1, the resulting quotient will neither be of the form 4n−1 nor have any prime factor of this form, unless perhaps both squares had such a common divisor, in which case the quotient would even contain the square of such a number.

items.quote: Ex ordine quotorum ergo, qui ſupra ex diuiſione ſummae binorum quadratorum per numerum primum formae $4n+1$ ſunt orti, excluduntur hi numeri
items.english: Hence from the sequence of quotients that arose above from dividing a sum of two squares by a prime of the form 4n+1, these numbers are excluded (3, 6, 7, 11, ...), and therefore only these remain (1, 2, 4, 5, 8, ...).
